name: GitHub
tagline: Register a GitHub OAuth App and plug it into Composio. No review, live in minutes.

steps.title: Set up your Composio account
steps.when: Skip if you already have a Composio project and API key.
instructions: Sign up from the Composio login page.
Open Settings → API keys and copy a key.
Save it as COMPOSIO_API_KEY where your agent runs.
Stay in this project. Auth configs belong to one project.

problems.q: I can't find the API keys page
a: Open the API keys link above after signing in. It opens Settings → API keys for your current project.
If you have several projects, switch to the one you'll use for this agent first.

steps.title: Choose who owns the app
instructions: Organization: survives team changes. You need the org owner role.
Personal account: fastest. You can transfer it to an org later.

warnings.text: Not an org owner? Register under your account now and transfer it to the org later.

steps.title: Register a new OAuth App
instructions: Open GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App.
For an org-owned app use github.com/organizations/<org>/settings/applications/new.
Fill in the form with the values below, then click Register application.
No review. The app works as soon as it's registered.

fields.label: Application name
fields.hint: Shown to users on the consent screen

fields.label: Authorization callback URL
fields.hint: Must match your Composio auth config exactly

fields.label: Enable Device Flow
fields.hint: Only for CLI or headless sign-in

warnings.text: Tokens now expire after 8 hours by default. Refresh tokens last 6 months if unused.
warnings.unconfirmed: Composio says it refreshes OAuth tokens. We didn't test GitHub's 8-hour tokens end to end.

problems.q: GitHub says redirect_uri_mismatch when a user connects
a: The callback URL in GitHub doesn't match the redirect URI in your Composio auth config.
Copy the value from your auth config and paste it into GitHub exactly, with no trailing slash.

steps.title: Generate a client secret
instructions: On the app page, click Generate a new client secret.
Copy it before leaving the page. GitHub shows it once.
Store it in a secret manager, never in git.
Note the Client ID too. It's public; the secret is not.

warnings.text: Lost the secret? Generate a new one and update your Composio auth config.

problems.q: I closed the page before copying the secret
a: You can't view it again. Generate a new secret on the same page.
Paste the new one into your Composio auth config, then delete the old one in GitHub.

steps.title: Check your Client ID
instructions: Paste your Client ID below. We open GitHub's sign-in page with it.
A valid ID makes GitHub say "continue to <your app name>". That's what your users will see.

problems.q: The check says GitHub doesn't recognise my ID
a: Make sure you copied the Client ID, not the client secret.
Check the app still exists under Developer settings → OAuth Apps.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
instructions: Open the GitHub toolkit in Composio and create an auth config.
Use the values below, then paste your Client ID and client secret.
Pick scopes from the GitHub tools your agent actually uses.
Save, then copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Must match the GitHub callback URL exactly

fields.label: Starter scopes
fields.hint: Trim to what your tools need

warnings.text: repo grants full read and write on every private repo. GitHub has no read-only private-repo scope.

steps.unconfirmed: The link exists. We couldn't check, without logging in, whether it opens auth config creation directly. If not: Auth Configs → Create Auth Config.

problems.q: The link didn't open the GitHub toolkit
a: Open Auth Configs in the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Pick GitHub, choose OAuth2, and turn on your own developer credentials.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
instructions: Pass the auth config ID when you create a session. Your coding agent can paste this in.
Toolkits you don't list keep using Composio's managed auth.

warnings.text: Check runs and check suites need a GitHub App. They fail with an OAuth App token.

a: The session must include authConfigs with your ac_… ID for github.
Toolkits not listed in authConfigs fall back to managed auth.

steps.title: Connect a test account
instructions: Start a connection for a test user and open the link.
The consent screen should show your app name, not Composio.
If an organization access section appears, grant or request access.
Users already connected through managed auth must reconnect.

warnings.text: GitHub keeps 10 tokens per user and scope set. The 11th connection revokes an older one.

steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run a full connection. It needs a Composio API key and a real GitHub sign-in.

problems.q: The consent screen still says Composio
a: The connection used the managed auth config. Pass your ac_… ID in the session.
Existing connections keep their old config. Delete and reconnect them.

problems.q: GitHub says the application is suspended
a: GitHub suspends apps over reported abuse or API misuse.
Only GitHub Support can lift it. Use Ask GitHub below.

steps.title: Get org approval
steps.when: Only if your users' GitHub orgs restrict OAuth apps. New orgs do by default.
instructions: Until approved, your users' private org repos stay hidden from your app.
Your user clicks Request next to the org on the consent screen.
An org owner approves it in the org's settings. GitHub sets no deadline.

problems.q: A user's private org repos are missing
a: Their org restricts OAuth apps. They need to click Request next to the org.
An org owner then approves your app in the org's settings.

wait.asStated: Up to the org owner. GitHub sets no deadline.

contacts.label: GitHub Support
contacts.when: Suspended apps, ownership transfers, or GitHub behaviour the docs don't explain.

contacts.label: Composio Discord
contacts.when: Auth config, connection, or tool errors inside Composio.
